questions.question: The requirements leave two kinds of entry open, so the tests cannot hold them either way (code B-6, input partitions no test takes). (a) Directly in the organized folder there can be entries that are neither a plain file nor a folder: a symbolic link (to a file, to a folder, or to nothing), and rarely a named pipe or socket; AC5 says only that folders are never moved. Should the run list them like files, or leave them in place like folders? (b) AC3 matches extensions without regard to case, but AC5 does not say so for the endings of files still being downloaded (.crdownload, .part, .download). Is a file such as report.pdf.PART a file still being downloaded, left in place, or a file listed to Others?
questions.recommended: (a) Leave every symbolic link and every entry that is not a plain file in place and unlisted, like folders, as the Mover moves by hard link and a hard link to a symbolic link acts differently on macOS and Linux, and a link to a folder moved would be a folder moved against AC5; (b) match those endings without regard to case, as AC3 does for extensions, since leaving a possibly unfinished download in place is the safe side and the user meets one rule for every ending.
